rites.name: Color
rites.text: Color is the ceaseless hue that bleeds through the sky of Lialintor during the third age of its mythic era, a concept that exists as a shimmering spectrum rather than a being. Those who attune to it can pull a single shade from the air and shape it into light, pigment, or force.

rites.name: Moreosia
rites.text: Moreosia is the concept of growth as it first takes shape in Lialintor, the rooting pulse that gathers loose sound into living stems during the Singing. It is less a being than a principle that the first sovereign's groves answered to, and it shapes the earliest kingdoms by teaching their roots where to reach.

rites.name: Thissora
rites.text: Thissora is a concept in Lialintor, a resonance held to be the sounding through which the first roots of the world condensed out of silence. Its name is spoken by the temple orders of the Holy Age as the measure of all beginnings, though no hand has ever recorded its exact form.

rites.name: Ashisteth
rites.text: Ashisteth is a concept of the Singing in Lialintor, the sounding by which the first roots of the world condense out of silence. It is a pure pattern of resonance rather than a being, felt as a rising note that thickens into matter wherever it passes. Temples of the Holy Age measure their hours by its return.

rites.name: Silium
rites.text: A forbidden book of arcane instruction that a wandering scholar wrote down for a single chilling tale. It teaches the careful releasing of a person's inner spirit from the body.

rites.name: Monus
rites.text: A ritual mark drawn by a writer whose tales of forbidden lore chronicle its use in a sorcerer's dealings with hidden powers. It is recorded across two chronicles of dreamers and scholars.

rites.name: Valosteror
rites.text: A short sung verse of fourteen lines, recited by devotees to call upon a sea-deity. It is written as a poem and carries the weight of a sacred incantation.

rites.name: Verostium
rites.text: A dark chanted ritual in which a verse-bound invocation is spoken to draw a slumbering toad-like entity from its hidden depths. The incantation is recorded in the form of a poem.

rites.name: Tintaulia
rites.text: A sacred tongue kept by a dying continent for chanting rites and binding spells. Its words are spoken aloud to work enchantments.

rites.name: Mistor
rites.text: A forbidden tome of sacred verses holds a summoning rite for sea-dwelling beings. These entities offer their callers wisdom, wealth, and the power to travel beyond the body, in return for loyalty to their masters.

rites.name: Brastuldeld
rites.text: Brastuldeld is a concept of the Lialintor Weave, the sleeping pattern of quiet powers that the makers planted during the Seeding. In the Holy Age, when flame, temples and orders hold sway, it is invoked as the pattern that binds burning vows to the land.

rites.name: Veniolwen
rites.text: Veniolwen is a concept of the Weave in Lialintor, the thread the makers laid down while quiet powers slept through the Seeding. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds, it was the pattern that held the scattered powers together.

rites.name: Ukataum
rites.text: Ukataum is a concept of Lialintor's Holy Age, personified as the flame that held the Pact together after the Sundering broke the worlds into Shards. Temple orders carried its name through the long fall, and its heat was said to be the last warmth of a dying sky.

rites.name: Eluannirla
rites.text: Eluannirla is a concept in Lialintor, the notion of a fall that split the old world into shards during the Sundering, when the Pact was sworn to bind the fragments. It is remembered as the moment landfall broke the old bonds between peoples and places. Its power is the weight of that breaking, felt wherever the Pact still holds.

rites.name: Amiallor Vausalus
rites.text: A short verse is composed as a means of calling forth a sleep-borne messenger. It is a brief chant, written to be spoken as an invocation.

rites.name: Lolum
rites.text: A shadowed rite is performed in a decaying coastal town, drawing on forbidden lore of the deep. It is staged as an interactive tale told through play.

rites.name: Valintium
rites.text: A printed manual of practical ritual magic, written by a single author and issued in several editions. It offers step-by-step instructions drawn from an invented body of forbidden lore.

rites.name: Contum
rites.text: A serialized tale of a restless scholar who forces dead bodies to rise through strange procedures, producing mindless, wild-tempered creatures. Its grim vision later inspired a famous screen adaptation and many other retellings.

rites.name: Sernaules
rites.text: A secret written and spoken speech that exists only in forbidden lore. It is said to pass between shadowy cults and the strange entities they serve, and it is thought to have entered the wider lore of dark occult texts.

rites.name: Cianosum
rites.text: A chanted verse of a shadowy cosmic faith, first circulated in a small dark-tales journal and later chosen by readers to close a collected volume of such writings.

rites.name: Sornilus
rites.text: A verse-form written as a devotional chant that bows before a vast cosmic presence. It is set down on the page as a poem in the traditions of a hidden lore.

rites.name: Valistarum
rites.text: A short tale of a hidden set of rules that governs a forbidden power. Its author is a writer of this invented world who recounts how its strange procedures were recorded.

rites.name: Sauntium
rites.text: Sauntium is the unspoken veil that drifted between the first silences of Lialintor, older than every choir except the two that made it. Its mist is said to swallow the names of stars, and no scribe has ever recorded its shape without erasing the page.

rites.name: Leontor
rites.text: Leontor is a coiled sky-serpent of the Lialintor cosmos, said to shed its scales as new stars when the old ones die. Its devotion to the broods it has spawned is so fierce that anyone who harms them is transformed into a reptile of the same color.

rites.name: Tiniarnes
rites.text: Tiniarnes is a sleeping sea-tyrant of the Mythic age, whose coral-bound body lies coiled beneath the drowned trenches of Lialintor. Its dreams alone raise tides that have swallowed whole archipelagos, and sailors chant its name backward to keep it from waking. Only the moon-forged harpoon of the Second Dynasty is said to be able to pin it again.

rites.name: Orasontanum
rites.text: Orasontanum is a drifting lattice of thought-glass that hangs between the hollow moons of Lialintor, feeding on the fading echoes of forgotten prayers. Its tenders claim it can reveal how any object folds through the seams of the hidden dimensions, though only in total silence. When unbound, its lattice spreads across the sky, slowly reshaping the nearby stars into quiet, dreaming shapes.

rites.name: Zephistasha
rites.text: Zephistasha is the concept of a branching ending, the moment in the Three Futures where Lialintor's story divides and every outcome is shelved in the Library. It is less a being than a fixed pressure that bends what can still happen, and it persists while the branches remain unchosen.

rites.name: Tenmalira
rites.text: Tenmalira is a concept in the Lialintor cycle, the idea that the ending branches into three futures and that a Library shelves each outcome as it forms. In the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, it is taught as the reason the orders keep their vigils: every choice is written before it is made.

rites.name: Thavsishora
rites.text: Thavsishora is the concept of a branching ending, the moment in Lialintor's Three Futures when a single fate splits into shelved outcomes within the Library. During the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders, it is invoked as the principle that every vow carries a second path waiting unspoken. Its presence is felt less as a force than as a quiet pressure on what is chosen.
